claims.statement: Tmall_SSH is a Struts2 2.5.14.1 + Spring 4.3.18 + Hibernate 5.3.7 + JSP storefront/admin application, and in this checkout it runs self-contained: running StartJetty.main() compiles the sources, starts embedded Jetty 9.4.58 on port 8080 against an H2 1.4.200 in-memory database, and serves the site with no external Tomcat or MySQL.

MIGRATION.md records the conversion's hard constraint - the original business Java (53 files by its own count), the JSPs, web.xml and the directory structure left unchanged and no framework version upgraded - and lists the only artifacts that conversion added or touched: the new src/StartJetty.java launcher, the three 【H2改造-N】 edit blocks in src/applicationContext.xml, the new src/sql/tmall_ssh_h2.sql, the newly populated web/WEB-INF/lib, and IDE/VCS metadata. That constraint is a migration-time freeze statement and no longer describes the whole working tree: the later spec-driven iteration scene2-product-remark modified three files inside the frozen set (src/com/caozhihu/tmall/pojo/Product.java, web/admin/listProduct.jsp, web/admin/editProduct.jsp) and appended a column to the adapted script, so the frozen set's 52-file membership is unchanged while its content is not.

The application source under src/com/caozhihu/tmall is divided into eight packages - action, service, service.impl, dao.impl, pojo, interceptor, util and test - while src/StartJetty.java and the wiring and seed resources (applicationContext.xml, struts.xml, log4j2.xml, sql/tmall_ssh_h2.sql) sit unpackaged at the root of src/.

Dependencies in the Java layers run one way only: the action layer depends solely on the service interfaces - Action4Service autowires the nine *Service interfaces and nothing below them - and no class under the action package imports com.caozhihu.tmall.dao or org.hibernate; ServiceDelegateDAO is the only non-test class that imports DAOImpl.

DAOImpl is the single persistence gateway: it is declared as the @Repository("dao") bean, extends Spring's HibernateTemplate, and overrides setSessionFactory with @Resource(name = "sf") to receive the SessionFactory bean; the project deliberately has no DAO interface.

BaseService declares the project's CRUD and paging vocabulary once (list, listByPage, total, listByParent, list(Page, parent), total(parent), save, delete, get, update, and a varargs pair-keyed list), BaseServiceImpl implements all of it with DetachedCriteria and HQL, and concrete interfaces such as ProductService extend BaseService and add only domain-specific methods.

BaseServiceImpl resolves the entity class it queries by reflection in its own constructor: it takes stackTrace[1] to learn the subclass name, strips the ServiceImpl suffix and rewrites '.service.impl' to '.pojo', so a *ServiceImpl class must share its entity's name and live in the service.impl package for queried methods to work.

ServiceDelegateDAO injects the single DAO bean by name (@Resource(name = "dao")) and forwards the whole HibernateTemplate API to it, which is what lets concrete services call HibernateTemplate methods such as findByCriteria directly instead of through dao.

Page is the shared pagination value object used by the service layer: it defaults to 5 rows per page and derives total pages and the last-page offset from start/count/total, and it is bound from the request through Action4Pagination.

Every HTTP endpoint in the application is an @Action-annotated method that returns a result name - 47 in total, 24 storefront (fore*) and 23 back office (admin_*) - because src/struts.xml declares no <action> element at all, so URLs and result mappings exist only in annotations.

The @Namespace("/"), @ParentPackage("basicstruts") and global @Results catalogue that maps result names to JSP paths and redirect targets live on the shared Action4Result base class, so the eight concrete action classes only contribute their @Action methods.

The Action4* inheritance chain splits what one action class would otherwise carry: Action4Upload holds the upload fields, Action4Pagination adds page, Action4Pojo adds the entities and their collections, Action4Service injects the services and provides t2p()/saveWithJpg(), Action4Parameter adds request-bound fields such as sort/keyword/num/oiid, and Action4Result adds the result catalogue.

t2p(Object) converts an id-only request-bound object into its persistent entity: it calls the matching service to load the entity by id and reflects the result back through the action's own setter (for example setCategory), so the field a JSP reads is fully populated before rendering.

web/WEB-INF/web.xml declares two filters mapped to /* (StrutsPrepareAndExecuteFilter with init-param contextConfigLocation=classpath:struts.xml, and Spring's CharacterEncodingFilter set to UTF-8) plus the context-param and ContextLoaderListener that load classpath:applicationContext.xml, and it declares no welcome-file-list.

src/struts.xml sets struts.objectFactory=spring so actions are Spring-managed beans, and defines the basicstruts package with three project interceptors (AuthInterceptor, CategoryNamesBelowSearchInterceptor, CartTotalItemNumberInterceptor) whose auth-dafault stack is installed as default-interceptor-ref, ordering all three before defaultStack for every action in the package.

AuthInterceptor only enforces login for request URIs starting with /fore: if no user object is in the session and the requested method is not in its allow-list (home, checkLogin, register, loginAjax, login, product, category, search), it sends a redirect to login.jsp; no admin_* URL enters that branch, so the 23 back office endpoints have no interceptor-level authentication gate.

Persistence is wired in src/applicationContext.xml: bean ds is a DriverManagerDataSource on jdbc:h2:mem:tmall_ssh;MODE=MySQL;DB_CLOSE_DELAY=-1, bean dbInit (DataSourceInitializer with a ResourceDatabasePopulator on classpath:sql/tmall_ssh_h2.sql) creates and seeds the schema at startup, and bean sf (LocalSessionFactoryBean) declares depends-on="dbInit", scans com.caozhihu.* and sets H2Dialect with hibernate.hbm2ddl.auto=none, so schema management belongs solely to the SQL script.

Spring is configured with context:annotation-config, component-scan base-package="com.caozhihu.tmall.*", and tx:annotation-driven bound to a HibernateTransactionManager named transactionManager that references bean sf; the component scan is what creates the action and service beans that Struts and the interceptors resolve by type and by name.

The pre-migration MySQL configuration (com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver datasource and a MySQL5Dialect session factory) is retained as a commented block at the end of src/applicationContext.xml as the documented switch-back path, and each H2 edit is tagged with a 【H2改造-N】 comment.

The nine persistence entities in com.caozhihu.tmall.pojo are mapped with JPA annotations (@Entity/@Table/@Id/@GeneratedValue, with @Transient for view-only fields) and are discovered by packagesToScan com.caozhihu.*, while the 9 business tables and their seed rows come from the adapted H2 script rather than from Hibernate DDL.

On every launch StartJetty compiles all .java files under src/ into web/WEB-INF/classes with the JDK compiler (UTF-8, -source/-target 8, web/WEB-INF/lib plus the classes dir on the classpath) and copies every non-Java resource there preserving relative paths, which is why classpath:applicationContext.xml, classpath:struts.xml and classpath:sql/tmall_ssh_h2.sql resolve and why the project needs no manual build step.

A request for the exact path / is rewritten to /forehome by an anonymous exact-match Rule installed on a Jetty RewriteHandler - deliberately not RewritePatternRule, whose prefix/regex semantics with pattern / would also rewrite every other path such as /img/**; web/index.jsp independently issues response.sendRedirect("/forehome") with an absolute path.

Because the same jars sit on both the JVM classpath and WEB-INF/lib, the launcher registers log4j, H2, JSP/Jasper and EL packages via addSystemClass and installs an explicit Configuration chain that includes AnnotationConfiguration, without which the JSP JasperInitializer never runs and JSP compilation fails with getTldCache() is null.

The H2 web console is started on its own port (8082) by org.h2.tools.Server.createWebServer instead of being mounted inside the 8080 web application, because the Struts2 filter mapped to /* would intercept an in-app console path and report no mapped action.

The view layer has two separate JSP surfaces with separate fragment sets: the ten web/admin/*.jsp list and edit screens each include ../include/admin/adminHeader.jsp and ../include/admin/adminNavigator.jsp (with ../include/admin/adminPage.jsp added by the five paged list screens), while the top-level web/*.jsp storefront pages include fragments from web/include such as include/header.jsp, include/top.jsp and include/footer.jsp.

Uploaded images are written into the exploded web application directory through ServletActionContext.getServletContext().getRealPath("img/...") and converted to JPEG with ImageUtil/ImageIO, then served as static files from web/img, so image state lives on the running webapp's file system rather than in the database.

The only automated test in the repository is src/com/caozhihu/tmall/test/TestTmall.java: a SpringJUnit4ClassRunner test configured with classpath:applicationContext.xml that autowires DAOImpl and runs two @Transactional Category operations.

MIGRATION.md records the measured acceptance of this variant on JDK 17: one-command start with no Tomcat or MySQL, HTTP 200 for /forehome and /admin_category_list, 200 for static resources, H2 console queries against the 9 business tables, auto-increment parity with the original MySQL (a new category gets id 84), and confirmed zero change to the existing business source.

MIGRATION.md's stated inventory over-counts the frozen business source: the document claims 53 original business Java files, while this checkout holds 52 .java files under src/com/**; the 53rd .java file in the repository is src/StartJetty.java, which the same document classifies as the one new, business-independent launcher class.

MIGRATION.md's dependency accounting is internally inconsistent and does not match the checkout: its change list says 65 jars were added, its dependency-section heading says 64, and web/WEB-INF/lib actually contains 65 jars.

STARTUP.md still lists the PROPERTYVALUE FOREIGN KEY(PID) referential-integrity message as a harmless startup warning, even though MIGRATION.md records it as eliminated by changing hibernate.hbm2ddl.auto from update to none and src/applicationContext.xml currently sets hibernate.hbm2ddl.auto=none for that reason, so STARTUP.md leads a reader to expect a log line that should no longer appear.

src/sql/tmall_ssh_h2.sql diverges from the original MySQL dump both syntactically and structurally: beyond the migration-time syntax adaptations, the scene2-product-remark iteration appended 'ALTER TABLE product ADD COLUMN remark varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL;' at line 155, between the product INSERT block and CREATE TABLE productimage, so the seeded product table no longer matches what the unchanged CREATE TABLE product at line 58 produces - while the script's header comment still lists only four syntactic adaptation points and still states that the business table structure and data were left unchanged.

The scene2-product-remark iteration's applied change set is exactly four existing files - src/com/caozhihu/tmall/pojo/Product.java, src/sql/tmall_ssh_h2.sql, web/admin/listProduct.jsp and web/admin/editProduct.jsp - with src/com/caozhihu/tmall/action/ProductAction.java, all service classes and the DAO deliberately left unmodified, which is why a newly persisted product field requires no action-layer or service-layer change in this codebase.

The product remark added by that iteration is an ordinary persisted property rather than render-only data: Product.java declares an unannotated String remark with getters/setters outside the @Transient block that holds firstProductImage, productSingleImages, productDetailImages, reviewCount and saleCount, and the admin product screens read and write it through the pre-existing OGNL property paths (product.remark in the list-page add form and the edit form, p.remark in the list column).
